featured.title: Aaron Levie · Box CEO
featured.summaryEn: Box CEO Aaron Levie posted a few sharp takes this week. The counterintuitive core: cheaper AI does NOT mean lower AI spend. Lower unit cost drives more consumption—you can now afford AI for a wider range of tasks, so you write more code, review more code for bugs and security, and run agents on datasets you couldn't process before; total spend goes up. On open source: in a world where open alternatives are only just behind the frontier, gatekeeping frontier access makes you less secure and less competitive—even if…
featured.insightZh: Box CEO Aaron Levie 这周连发几条，核心是「AI 变便宜 ≠ AI 支出下降」这个反直觉判断。他的逻辑：成本下降会刺激消费，而不是抑制——一旦单位成本降低，你就能把 AI 用到之前用不起的任务上，写更多代码、审更多代码、跑更多此前处理不动的大数据集，总支出反而上升。他还给开源模型算了笔账：在开源已经贴近前沿的世界里，靠「卡住前沿模型访问权」来自保只会让你更不安全、更没竞争力——就算美国能全面禁掉开源模型，别的生态系统没这个禁令，反而拿到了访问优势。另一条谈 AI 扩散：AI 驱动的进步最终会被「它与现实世界的交互」限速——编程之所以被快速采用，正因为你可以近乎无限地写代码、测试、运行并产生价值，全程不需要外部世界的任何人改变行为。

featured.title: Zara Zhang · Builder、内容创作者
featured.summaryEn: Builder Zara Zhang surfaced an idea that's becoming consensus: code/software can now be disposable. Her examples of things discarded right after use—spinning up a design playground/modal to fine-tune the look and feel of a UI; generating HTML pages just to understand some code; standing up a throwaway dashboard to inspect something once. These aren't assets to maintain; they're tools you toss. Her content-positioning tip: if you're starting on social and don't know what to talk about, ask what the top 3 questions…
featured.insightZh: Builder Zara Zhang 提了一个正在成为共识的观念：代码/软件现在可以是「一次性」的。她举了几个用完即弃的例子——为自己搭个设计 playground/弹窗来微调某个界面的观感；生成一堆 HTML 页面帮自己理解代码；临时起一个仪表盘只为看一眼某个数据。这类东西不再是需要长期维护的资产，而是用完就丢的工具。另一条讲个人内容定位：想开始做社媒但不知道聊什么，就想「朋友/同事最常问你的 top 3 问题是什么」，把答案照你当面回答的口吻做成视频/帖子——如果一件事你反复讲过 3 次以上，那就是你的定位。

featured.title: Stripe AI 负责人：AI Agent 将如何买、卖与支付
featured.summaryEn: Agentic commerce has moved from last year's "purely hypothetical" to deployed infrastructure with real brands on it—but the most underdiscussed risk isn't overspending or buying the wrong thing; it's token theft, with more than one in six signups at AI companies being this kind of "dine and dash for tokens" abuse. Guest Emily Sense (Head of Data & AI at Stripe) frames agentic commerce as a full spectrum: at one end, agents autonomously discover a service, decide to buy, and settle the transaction with no human in the loop (Stripe's Machine Payments Protocol, MPP); at the other, a person asks inside an AI surface for "shoes for flat-footed runners," and the answer increasingly comes with a buy button. Consumers today mostly hover at "level 2"—delegating a little selection or leaning hard on AI to find products, with hints of level 3, but nowhere near one-shotting a whole summer vacation…

items.title: Cat Wu · Anthropic Claude Code + Cowork
items.summaryEn: Cat Wu (Claude Code + Cowork at Anthropic) shared her practical prompt for using Claude Cowork to manage her calendar—worth copying directly: manage her week with constraints of under 20 hours of meetings; dedupe conflicting meetings; look at past weeks to learn which meetings she declines; dinners don't count against the 20 hours; build a skill that gets refined over time; and ask before updating invites. The value isn't "AI runs my calendar" but the reusable pattern: personal preferences + constraints + an itera…
items.insightZh: Anthropic 做 Claude Code 和 Cowork 的 Cat Wu 分享了她用 Claude Cowork 管日历的实用 prompt，值得直接抄：要求 Cowork 帮她安排一周日程，约束条件是——每周会议少于 20 小时；对冲突会议去重；参考过去几周看她通常会拒掉哪类会议；晚餐不计入 20 小时额度；把这套逻辑沉淀成一个可迭代的 skill；更新邀请前先问她。这条的价值不在「AI 管日历」本身，而在于把「个人偏好 + 约束条件 + 可迭代 skill + 人在环确认」打包成一个可复用模式。

items.title: Peter Yang · AI 教程创作者
items.summaryEn: AI tutorial creator Peter Yang spent the week stress-testing ChatGPT Work / Codex, with useful gripes. He notes non-technical ChatGPT Work users don't know what "run this chat in the cloud" even means; on Codex it told him to send to Codex Web, then clicking the link just told him to download the app again—his one-liner: "Copy matters." For teams building agent products, this is a direct signal: no matter how capable the model, if the entry-point copy and mental-model barrier aren't cleared, non-technical users si…
items.insightZh: AI 教程创作者 Peter Yang 这周在实测 ChatGPT Work / Codex 的产品体验，几条吐槽挺有价值。他指出用 ChatGPT Work 的非技术用户根本不懂「run this chat in the cloud（在云端运行这个对话）」是什么意思；在 Codex 里让他发到 Codex Web，点了链接却又叫他再下一次 app——他一句话点破：copy matters（文案很重要）。这类来自真实高频用户的产品细节反馈，对做 agent 产品的团队是很直接的信号：能力再强，入口文案和心智门槛没跨过，非技术用户就是用不起来。

items.title: Dan Shipper · Every CEO
items.summaryEn: Every CEO Dan Shipper reported a threshold moment: over the past week, AI has been able to automatically do ~70% of the copy edits his team @every would normally do by hand internally—the first time that's happened, after years of trying. For content and media teams, it's a concrete productivity signal: copy editing, long assumed to require human polish, is hitting an inflection where AI can take over a large share.
items.insightZh: Every CEO Dan Shipper 报告了一个「跨过临界点」的时刻：过去一周，AI 已经能自动完成他们内部原本靠人工手改的约 70% 文案编辑工作——这是头一回做到，而他试了好几年。对做内容/媒体的团队，这是个具体的生产力信号：文案编辑这类长期被认为「必须人来精修」的环节，正在到达可被 AI 大比例接管的拐点。

items.title: Amjad Masad · Replit CEO
items.summaryEn: Replit CEO Amjad Masad offered an observation on consumer subscription businesses: consumers spend on food, rent, entertainment, phone & internet, and shopping—software is typically bought by their companies. That's why, outside of Netflix, Spotify, etc., it's hard to think of truly *huge* consumer subscription businesses. Useful for gauging the ceiling of consumer AI products: to become a giant, a B2C subscription has to land in the categories (entertainment or necessities) where consumers already pay out of pock…
items.insightZh: Replit CEO Amjad Masad 抛了一个关于消费者订阅生意的观察：消费者花钱在食物、房租、娱乐、话费网费、购物上，软件通常是他们所在的公司买单——这就是为什么除了 Netflix、Spotify 这类之外，很难想到真正*巨型*的消费者订阅生意。这条对判断 AI 消费级产品的天花板有参考价值：C 端订阅要长成巨头，得挤进「娱乐」或「刚需」这几个消费者本来就愿意自掏腰包的品类。

items.title: Guillermo Rauch · Vercel CEO
items.summaryEn: Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch made a counterintuitive call: he's very bullish on cybersecurity as one of the best benchmarks for superintelligence—the "IQ test" of software engineering. His reasoning: it's actually easy for a model to "one-shot an XYZ clone" and impress people on X, but that's not a good test; the hard part is finding, patching, reversing, and exploiting. He notes the best engineers he's worked with usually had a deep security background or interest. A worthwhile yardstick for anyone assessing the ce…
items.insightZh: Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch 给了个反常识的判断：他非常看好网络安全作为衡量超级智能的最佳基准之一——把它称为软件工程的「IQ 测试」。理由是让模型「一把梭克隆一个 XYZ」去 X 上博眼球其实很容易，但那不是好测试；真正难的是发现、修补、逆向、利用漏洞。他观察到自己职业生涯里合作过的最优秀工程师，往往都有很深的安全背景或兴趣。对评估 AI coding 能力上限的人，这是个值得记下的标尺。

items.title: Garry Tan · Y Combinator CEO
items.summaryEn: YC president & CEO Garry Tan flagged a trending take: Markdown files are universal and will survive millennia, and unsurprisingly they're a fantastic data format when the intelligence stack is in flux at this extreme pace. He also teased "GSkills." For anyone building agent memory/skill systems, this echoes a practical consensus—plain text/markdown as an agent's persistence layer is more change-resistant than locking into a proprietary format.
items.insightZh: YC 总裁兼 CEO Garry Tan 点了一个正在流行的判断：Markdown 文件是通用的、能存活千年，在智能栈以极快速度变动的当下，它意外地成了一种极佳的数据格式。他还顺手抛了个「GSkills」的钩子。对正在搭 agent 记忆/skill 体系的人，这条呼应了一个实践共识——用纯文本/markdown 作为 agent 的持久层，比锁进某个专有格式更耐变。
